text:
sam: RFC follow-up: staged decryption + partial rollback for huge model shards in air-gapped installs. goal: minimize peak disk + reduce restart downtime when swapping models. outline below, PTAL.

rebecca: high-level? sounds promising — how does staging differ from current 'download then activate' dance?

sam: current: agent downloads full bundle, verifies sig, decrypts in-place, atomically swaps. problem: decrypting multi-10s-100s GB requires 2x disk and long outage. staged decrypt: stream-decrypt shards into a separate content-store and mark them CANDIDATE. once all critical shards are CANDIDATE and checks pass, we flip a small activation marker. no big copy/swap.

tony: streaming decryption ok, but we need integrity checks per-shard. want Merkle/strong hash per-shard and a manifest with shard map.

sam: yes. manifest additions: shards: [{id, size, sha256, merkle_root, encrypted:true, cipher_meta}]. agent verifies per-shard hash after decrypt. also support partial activation: activate only "core_shards" first to allow lightweight traffic while background-async loads noncritical shards.

rebecca: core_shards concept is interesting. how defined? model maintainers tag shards with priority: P0 (runtime), P1 (recommended), P2 (optional). operator can override.

sam: operator CLI: `rctl model promote --id <id> --priority-cutoff P1 --grace 60s`. agent will attempt to ensure all shards <= cutoff are CANDIDATE, run local probes, then set active_model_id. other shards pulled lazily.

eng-bot: note: add metrics: model_stage_bytes_decrypted, model_activation_latency_seconds, model_lazy_fetch_failures_total.

sre: network/airgap nuance: on air-gapped nodes we often transfer via host appliance. appliance will push shards; should we change appliance protocol?

sam: appliance should push shard-by-shard and include resume tokens. propose API: POST /v1/shards/{model_id}/{shard_id}?offset=... with Content-Range semantics. agent writes to staging file, computes streaming MAC, and can resume.

tony: resume tokens must be cryptographically tied to shard to prevent replay. HMAC(shard_id|model_id|offset|nonce). appliance keeps the nonce.

rebecca: what about disk pressure? if staging store full, agent should evict non-candidate old models. eviction policy: LRU by last_access + pinned models. also ability to throttle decryption to avoid OOM spikes.

sam: yes: agent config: staging_capacity_bytes, decrypt_concurrency (default 2), low_disk_threshold_pct. Agent will stop new decrypts if free < threshold.

security: decrypt keys live in KMS, but air-gapped onprem might use operator-provided key blobs. Need explicit key-unseal step with operator approval.

sam: propose key-unseal API `POST /v1/unseal-keys` that takes sealed key envelope. operator runs CLI against bastion to unseal. agent stores keys in an encrypted local keystore (OS-level). keys have TTL and must be refreshed for large decrypt operations.

rebecca: TTL could cause long decrypts to fail mid-stream. support key-reauth/resume: if TTL expires, agent pauses decrypt, requests new unseal, resumes with stored offset.

tony: partial rollback story? if new model activation causes bad behavior we must revert quickly to prior model w/o pulling everything again.

sam: activation markers: active_model_id + activated_shards_list. keep previous_active_model_id and a compact reverse-index of previous shards locations. On rollback, set active_model_id back, and agents can lazily fetch any missing previous shards from local cache or request appliance resync. No blocking restart.

sre: but if previous model shards were garbage collected, operator rollback may need to re-push via appliance. add operator-visible status `rollback_requires_resync: true`.

eng-bot: add alerting: model_activation_failure_rate > 0.05 over 10m -> P2. lazy_fetch_failures_total > 10 -> paging.

security: threat model: streaming decrypt could be MITM if appliance compromised. ensure envelope includes shard HMACs and signed manifest; agent verifies both before accepting next shard. also require appliance auth via cert pinned to operator.

sam: agreed. manifest must be signed and include per-shard signature or merkle proofs. agent will reject shards not covered by manifest.

rebecca: operator UX: need a 'dry-run' promote that stages shards on a small canary subset and runs smoke checks. propose `rctl model promote --canary 3` to stage on 3 nodes first then proceed.

tony: canary needs isolation: we should annotate canary nodes in operator manifest or via labels. rollout planner uses those labels.

sre: monitoring: add `model_stage_progress{node,model,shard}` gauge. also expose `staged_shards_percent`.

sam: perf: decrypt concurrency default 2, measured with k8s nodes: decrypting 300GB across 4 cores ~ 12-18 minutes with AES-NI and fast disks. will put numbers in RFC.

security: final note on key rotation: add key_version in manifest and allow agents to retain older key versions for rollback decryption for a grace window. operator must orchestrate rotation across cluster.

rebecca: docs, runbooks, and appliance changes needed. can you add a migration plan for older installs where manifest lacks shard metadata?

sam: migration: older bundles treated as single-shard with priority P0. agent falls back to legacy path for those models. I'll include upgrade compatibility matrix.

tony: LGTM. please add example manifest snippet and the appliance HTTP range example in the RFC addendum.

sam: will do. I'll post full addendum with schema + example CLI flows + metrics + runbook in 72h. tagging @rebecca @tony @sre @security for review. :white_check_mark:
